sources.title: Chat statement (2026-09-21): IT support takes 5 days; Ana owns it

sections.title: Stated cycle time: 5 days (measure and period not stated)

decisions.question: Confirm the pilot choice: IT support (owned by Ana) rather than Purchasing (shorter cycle, no owner). The request asked for the fastest process; the recommendation ranks ownership above cycle time. Does the sponsor accept?
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the sources)

decisions.question: What event opens an IT support request (email, phone, walk-up, ticket) and what observable condition closes it (requester confirms, Ana closes, no reply after N days)?

Is the stated 5-day IT support duration an observed average, a median, a typical case or a worst case, over which period, and measured in calendar days or workdays? It is recorded as a stated value, not a measured baseline, until answered.

How many IT support requests arrive per month, and which request types (access, hardware, software, other) are most frequent? The pilot needs enough real cases to review after several completions; no volume was supplied and none was assumed.
Who handles IT support requests besides Ana (technicians, an external provider), and who covers when Ana is absent? Needed before the designer can assign actions to a group rather than to one person.
Will management name a Purchasing owner? Purchasing stays a candidate for the second workflow only once someone accepts ownership of approvals, exceptions and the review of results.
decisions.owner: Pilot sponsor (not named in the sources)
